title: Payment Operations Specialist, Technical Operations
description:
About FastSpring :

FastSpring is how AI, SaaS, gaming, software, and digital product companies sell online in more places around the world. We handle all payment needs from checkout to taxes so you can go farther faster.

Founded in 2005, we are a privately owned company headquartered in Santa Barbara with offices in Amsterdam, Austin, Belfast, Dublin, Halifax, and Singapore.

Payment Operations Specialist, Technical Operations
Department: Payment Operations | Location: Remote - United States | Reports To: Senior Manager, Payment Operations
Position Overview:
The Payment Operations Specialist, Technical Operations supports daily payment operations across multiple processors and regions for FastSpring 's network of more than 2,500 sellers. The role pairs hands-on operational work - chargeback and PayPal dispute support, issue investigation, and seller-facing resolution - with technical operations analytics across five areas: authorization rates, chargeback rates, data normalization, processing costs, and reconciliation support. It is an entry-to-early-career position for someone curious about how payments work, comfortable in a spreadsheet, and inclined to chase down a number that looks wrong.
Within a year, this person should own recurring analysis in at least one of those five areas, handle disputes independently, and be the person others ask when a number doesn't reconcile - a path that leads toward senior payment operations, payments analytics, or risk and fraud. Payments is a field you learn by doing, and we welcome candidates from varied backgrounds and career paths; curiosity and analytical instinct matter more here than a specific résumé.
Responsibilities & Goals:

• Support chargeback and PayPal dispute workflows - case review, evidence gathering, and representment preparation under guidance from senior team members - and coordinate with sellers and internal teams to collect supporting documentation.

• Monitor chargeback volumes, win rates, and fraud ratios against card network thresholds by seller, processor, and MID, and analyze disputes by reason code, product, and geography to separate fraud from service or billing causes.

• Investigate Tier I-II payment inquiries involving authorizations, declines, settlements, refunds, disputes, or processor behavior; escalate complex cases and maintain clear handoff notes, including for weekend coverage.

• Track authorization approval and decline rates across processors, regions, and payment methods, breaking declines down by response code and category to pinpoint where approvals are being lost.

• Normalize payment data across sources - processor response codes, decline and chargeback categories, and reporting definitions - and run routine data-quality checks so figures from different systems are comparable.

• Track what payments actually cost by processor and region - interchange, scheme fees, acquirer markup, FX, and dispute fees - and check processor invoices and fee statements against expected rates, flagging anomalies or misapplied pricing.

• Support daily and monthly reconciliation across platform records, processor reports, and bank statements, investigating unmatched items and contributing to the reporting and SOPs that surface payment performance, cost, and dispute trends across the organization.

Experience & Qualifications:

• 1+ years of experience in payment operations, chargebacks, risk operations, customer support operations, finance operations, ecommerce operations, or a related field; experience in SaaS, digital goods, ecommerce, fintech, marketplace, or subscription businesses is a plus.

• Basic understanding of card payments, payment processors, PayPal, refunds, disputes, or the chargeback lifecycle; hands-on experience and exposure to merchant-of-record environments are preferred but not required.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Samsara is looking for a Senior Escalations Program Manager to own our most complex customer escalations and turn those experiences into durable improvements. Approximately 70% of your time will be spent managing complex customer finance requests, you will coordinate cross-functional resources, lead executive-level communications, and drive rapid, high-quality resolution for high-severity customer issues. The remaining 30% of your time will focus on programs that eliminate root causes, streamline workflows, proactively resolve potential customer billing issues and scale customer-facing processes.

This role is ideal for a structured, customer-centered operator who can bring clarity to complex situations, build alignment across teams, and translate individual escalations into systemic improvements.

• You’re energized by our opportunity: Digitizing large sectors of the global economy requires creative problem-solving, sound judgment, and a strong commitment to customer success.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, support each other, and hold ourselves accountable to high standards.

• Lead cross-functional programs to improve the customer experience - standardize escalation workflows, service-level expectations, tooling, reporting, and dashboards.

• Coach frontline teams on escalation prevention, de-escalation, customer communication, and effective use of escalation processes.

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles-Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, and Win as a Team-as we scale globally and across new offices.

title: Senior Clinical Research Associate - Oncology

We’re a global, midsize CRO that pushes boundaries, innovates and invents because the path to a cure for the world’s most persistent diseases is not paved by those who play it safe. It is built by those who take pioneering, creative approaches and implement them with quality and excellence.
We are Worldwide Clinical Trials , and we are a global team of over 3,500+ experts, bright thinkers, dreamers and doers and, together, we are changing the way the world experiences CROs - in the best possible way.
Our mission is to work with passion and purpose every day to improve lives and we are looking for others who value this same pursuit.
Why Worldwide
We believe everyone plays an important role in making a world of difference for patients and their caregivers. From our hands-on, accessible leaders, to our cohesive and supportive teams, we are committed to enabling professionals from all backgrounds and experiences to succeed. We prioritize cultivating a diverse and inclusive environment that continues to promote collaboration and creativity. We are proud to be a workplace where people thrive by being themselves and are inspired to do their best work every day. Join us!
What Clinical Operations does at Worldwide
At Worldwide Clinical Trials , we invite you to embark on a rewarding journey within Clinical Operations, where your contributions will leave a profound impact on the lives of patients.
As a Clinical Research Associate (CRA) at Worldwide, you will find yourself working alongside brilliant minds across diverse therapeutic areas, including Cardiovascular, Metabolic, Neuroscience, Oncology, and Rare Diseases. Through regular touchpoints and coaching conversations with your Line Manager, we ensure that your professional development remains a top priority. We offer a clear career path and development that can lead to Clinical Trial Manager roles. We take pride in our accessible Executive Leadership team, who are equally committed to advancing science and surmounting obstacles to make a difference in the lives of patients around the world.
We offer an unparalleled experience, where you can drive remarkable scientific breakthroughs and be at the very core of every successful clinical trial. Experience a world of difference with us at Worldwide!
What you will do

• Responsible for managing the research activities at sites participating in Worldwide’s clinical research projects

• Typically involved in all stages of the clinical study, including identifying potential sites to participate in the research effort, performing various study start-up activities such as working with sites to collect appropriate regulatory documents and supporting the negotiation of contracts and budgets, training the sites to collect data properly and report any potential safety-related events, managing the site's activities during study maintenance, and closing down research activities at the sites once the study has concluded

• While most of the site management efforts will be performed remotely, you will be required to ensure compliance with obtaining informed consent, reporting potential safety-related events, and adhering to all applicable regulatory requirements

What you will bring to the role

• Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills in English

• Superior organizational skills with attention to detail

• Ability to work with little or no supervision

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, CTMS, and EDC Systems

Your experience

• 5+ years of experience as a Clinical Research Ass

DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

- Ein klarer Entwicklungspfad: Von Junior- über Senior- und bis hin zu Führungsrollen..

- Eigenverantwortliche Wochenplanung und Vertrauensarbeitszeit.

- Firmenwagen inkl. Tankkarte sowie MacBook und iPhone.

- 50 € steuerfreies Guthaben pro Monat über Probonio.

- Fixgehalt und ungedeckelte Provision.

WIE GEHT ES WEITER?

1. Bewerbung & Sichtung - wir melden uns so schnell wie möglich bei dir.

2. Erstgespräch mit unserem Recruiting-Team (ca. 30-45 Minuten).

3. Video-Call mit deiner künftigen Führungskraft.

4. Field Day - zwei Stunden bei uns im Office. Du siehst, wie wir arbeiten, wir sehen dich in Aktion.

5. Abschlussgespräch mit unserer Head of Sales.

Salonkee steht für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Fähigkeiten - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Alter, Behinderung, Religion oder Identität.

title: Senior Major Gifts Officer
description:
About Spark

Spark is a science-driven, philanthropically funded non-profit that accelerates progress on unsolved climate challenges. Our goal is to enable a safer climate by filling targeted gaps in current climate actions. We look around the corner at the key blind spots that pose big climate risks or offer big climate opportunities, like major sources of unabated emissions. Then we work to speed up the development of the fields needed to address those challenges.

We are a team of scientists, policy experts, innovators, and systems thinkers working to build today’s foundations for the comprehensive climate solutions we will need tomorrow. Rather than betting on individual pathways or innovations, we work to grow a field as a whole so that the most effective science and solutions can be surfaced and scaled. We use a large suite of field-building tools to support new research, markets, policies, and talent development, through both in-house initiatives and building broader coalitions. We are currently focused on super pollutants from agriculture (specifically methane and nitrous oxide), warming-induced greenhouse gas emissions, and methane removal.

Spark’s impact is made possible by a community of generous and pioneering individuals, foundations, and organizations that share our vision for a safer climate future.

Position Summary

Spark is looking for a Senior Gifts Officer to build and deepen Spark's relationships with major and principal donors. This is a frontline fundraising role for someone who thrives on relationship-driven work, can effectively direct the rhythm and flow of funder relationships, and brings organization and diligence to the fundraising process. We’re looking for someone who is deeply comfortable working alongside scientists and researchers and who knows how to translate their work and leverage their ideas to attract funders.

You'll report to our Executive Director and work closely with our Program Directors to steward relationships and close gifts that move Spark’s fields forward. You’ll act as a connective node across our development and program teams-mapping funder interests to the right programs, coaching program directors ahead of funder meetings, making sure the right ask reaches the right funder at the right time, and owning follow-up steps with funders to bring grants through their process.

What You'll Do

• Attend funder meetings alongside executive leadership and program leads and identify, document, and drive the next steps

• Coach program directors on how to communicate with and engage funders more effectively over time

• Coordinate funder strategy across Spark’s programs-mapping funders to programs, clarifying relationship owners, and sequencing the right ask from the right program at the right time

• Close funding opportunities by understanding each donor’s perspective, portfolio, and knowing when and how to make the ask, and managing grant proposal steps and timelines.

• Steward funder relationships individually-tracking each funder’s interests and what they respond to, and matching Spark’s latest wins, research, and communications products to the right moments for engagement

• Work directly with scientists and program leads to translate complex research into compelling philanthropic narratives

• Prepare high-quality funder materials including briefings, proposals, reports, and stewardship updates

• Represent Spark at field convenings, donor events, and conferences

• Maintain rigorous CRM hygiene and contribute to pipeline reporting and forecasting

What We're Looking For

• 7+ years of frontline fundraising experience or comparable sales or business-development experience, with a track record of closing six- and seven-figure deals

• Experience building a portfolio of new relationships in a growth-stage or start-up environment

• Proven experience working in or alongside scientific, research, or technical organizations and the ability to partner with subject matter experts

title: Senior Software Engineer, Vehicle Interaction
description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver-The World's Most Experienced Driver™-to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Vehicle Interaction team tackles critical autonomous driving challenges, directly responsible for modeling agent interactions with other vehicles to advance our mission of safety and building the world's most trusted driver. The team develops agent reasoning and motion planning algorithms to resolve complex interactive scenarios-including lane changes, merges, unprotected maneuvers, and cut-ins. • Collaborate cross-functionally at the intersection of prediction and planning, leveraging large-scale models to solve complex agent interaction problems.

• Integrate learned models into closed-loop simulation environments, benchmark against rigorous safety metrics, and drive seamless transitions to production releases.

• Focus on high-impact product outcomes, making pragmatic engineering decisions to accelerate the shift from rule-based heuristics to scalable, data-driven policies.

You have:

• BS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 5+ years of software engineering experience developing high-performance, efficient C++ code.

• Hands-on experience building ML models, including expertise in learned driving policies (RL/imitation learning), PyTorch or JAX, closed-loop simulation evaluation, and a proven track record of shipping models to production.

• Proven capability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional engineering teams.

We prefer:

• MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field.

• Demonstrated software engineering expertise in motion planning or related autonomous systems problems.

• Experience building, training, and benchmarking machine learning systems at scale.

• Technical leadership experience guiding engineers or leading small project teams.

title: Senior Manager, Occupancy Planning & Workplace Strategy

We partner closely with business leaders, Finance, People, Workplace Operations, and Design & Construction to anticipate growth, optimize space utilization, and deliver a thoughtful, scalable workplace experience.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Occupancy Planning & Workplace Strategy Manager to lead strategic space planning for our Go-to-Market (GTM) and General & Administrative (G&A) organizations.

In this role, you’ll translate evolving business needs into actionable occupancy strategies, capacity scenarios, and workplace recommendations. You’ll serve as a trusted partner to business leaders, balancing growth projections, operational requirements, and employee experience to inform decisions about how our teams use space.

You’ll own planning across a complex, evolving portfolio while leveraging CAFM/IWMS systems and data analytics to drive accurate, scalable decision-making. This role requires a combination of strategic thinking, hands-on technical expertise, and strong cross-functional partnership to turn planning recommendations into operational outcomes.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week, with approximately 10-20% travel.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

- Own strategic occupancy planning for GTM and G&A organizations, translating headcount forecasts, business priorities, and workplace needs into actionable space plans.

- Develop and evaluate capacity scenarios, neighborhood strategies, team adjacencies, seating models, and space allocation recommendations to support organizational growth.

- Partner with business leaders and executive stakeholders to understand evolving requirements, communicate trade-offs, and align workplace strategies with business objectives.

- Collaborate with Finance, People, Analytics, Design & Construction, and Workplace Operations to reconcile forecasts, assess capacity constraints, and guide planning decisions through implementation.

- Translate workplace needs into practical stacking, blocking, and move plans, ensuring recommendations account for operational feasibility, timing, and employee experience.

- Leverage CAFM/IWMS platforms and analytical tools to maintain accurate space inventories, floor plans, seating allocations, and utilization data.

- Identify and resolve space data discrepancies, establish quality controls, and partner with internal system owners and external vendors to improve data reliability.

- Develop dashboards, planning workflows, and reporting tools that improve visibility into occupancy trends, capacity risks, and portfolio performance.

- Drive continuous improvement in occupancy planning processes, including opportunities for automation, system enhancements, and scalable planning practices.

- Support workplace change initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams to ensure clear communication, coordinated execution, and successful transitions.

title: Marketplace Pricing Scientist (6 months contract)
description:
About the role
Our dynamic pricing is rule-based today - conditional logic on surface signals like weather and supply-demand ratios. It works, but it's rigid, and we think it's leaving money on the table.
Our platform team is strong on data engineering and business analysis. What we don't have in-house is the applied economics or algorithmic depth to work out which pricing models are actually right for us. Other platforms have solved versions of this already. We want someone who can tell us which approach fits, prove it on our data, and hand it to our engineers to build.
6-month contract, fully remote and open to candidates anywhere , reporting to the Director, Platform.
What you will deliver

• A read on our existing pricing logic, with a number on the revenue and matching efficiency we're currently giving up

• A shortlist of approaches - mechanism design (VCG-style allocation), algorithmic search (optimal tree search, MCTS), predictive and ML pricing models - weighed against our data maturity, latency limits and commercial goals

• A recommended model, tested offline on GoGoX order and supply data, with the assumptions and failure modes spelled out

• An experiment design for live testing, including guardrails against cannibalising users or driver-partners, and the metrics that call it a win

• A handover pack our data engineers can build from, plus an honest view of what we'd need to hire or train for to own this long term

Who you are

• 5+ years applying economic or optimisation modelling to pricing, matching or incentives in a live two-sided marketplace - ride-hailing, logistics, delivery, travel or e-commerce

• Comfortable across mechanism design, causal inference (diff-in-diff, regression discontinuity, synthetic control), demand elasticity and structural modelling, and modern ML approaches to pricing

• Strong in Python and SQL, and happy working in production data next to engineers rather than handing over a paper

• Master's or PhD in Economics, Operations Research, Statistics or similar - or the industry track record that stands in for it

• Pragmatic about constraints. You recommend what works with the data and engineering we have, not what's most elegant

• Can explain the economics to a commercial audience. We can't act on a recommendation we can't interrogate

• Fluent spoken Cantonese

title: Cloud Network Engineer
description:
Cloud Network Engineer - Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Cloud Network Engineer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000-$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 10+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary:
We are seeking a Cloud Networking Engineer to design, deploy, and operate cloud networking infrastructure across one or more major cloud providers. The role covers VPC/VNet design, hybrid connectivity, transit topologies, edge networking, DNS, and the security controls that make cloud networking reliable and safe at scale. The ideal candidate combines deep traditional networking knowledge with cloud-native networking patterns, has built production cloud networks at meaningful scale, and brings strong automation discipline to networking work. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners - product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders - to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and operate cloud networking architectures including VPC/VNet, subnets, routing, and security groups.

• Build transit hub topologies using AWS Transit Gateway, Azure Virtual WAN, or GCP Network Connectivity Center.

• Design and implement hybrid connectivity using Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect, and VPN.

• Architect edge networking including CDN, global load balancing, and WAF integration.

• Implement DNS strategies including Route 53, Azure DNS, or Cloud DNS with hybrid resolution.

• Design private connectivity to managed services using PrivateLink, Private Endpoints, or Private Service Connect.

• Automate cloud networking with Terraform, providing infrastructure-as-code coverage across the network estate.

• Implement network security controls including firewalls, NACLs, security groups, and DDoS protection.

• Operate Kubernetes networking including CNI selection, ingress strategies, and service exposure patterns.

• Build observability for cloud networking including flow logs, traffic insights, and packet capture.

• Drive cost optimization including data transfer reduction and right-sizing of network resources.

• Partner with security teams to harden the network perimeter and enforce zero-trust principles.

• Troubleshoot complex cloud networking issues across cloud and hybrid environments.

• Stay current with cloud networking platform updates and emerging patterns.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Networking, or a related field.

• Ten or more years of experience in networking, with significant time on cloud networking.

• Deep hands-on experience with networking on at least one major cloud provider.

• Strong understanding of routing, switching, BGP, and modern networking fundamentals.

• Hands-on experience with hybrid connectivity (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, or equivalents).

• Experience with infrastructure-as-code for cloud networking, especially Terraform.

• Strong understanding of cloud security and network controls.

• Familiarity with Kubernetes networking and service mesh fundamentals.

• Strong troubleshooting and packet-level analysis skills.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

The Role
As our Cyber Risk and Compliance Specialist, you will occupy a critical role that is 50% technical auditor and 50% security advocate. You will ensure the integrity of our financial systems through IT SOX compliance while simultaneously maturing our global compliance posture (HIPAA/NIS2) and building a high-integrity security culture through a comprehensive Security Awareness program.

Focus A: IT SOX & Financial Integrity (60%)

•
Program Ownership : Lead the IT SOX program and design, implement, and test IT General Controls (ITGCs), IT Application controls (ITACs) and Key Reports (IPE) across our enterprise applications, databases, and infrastructure.

• Deficiency Management: Lead the root-cause analysis for any control failures and partner with stakeholders to build long-term, remediation plans.

Focus B: HIPAA, NIS2 & Risk Advisory (30%)
• Healthcare Compliance (HIPAA): Act as the technical SME for the HIPAA Security Rule, ensuring controls protect PHI, including controls monitoring and providing guidance to management for new systems.

• Culture Building: Design targeted communication campaigns to increase internal reporting of security incidents and reinforce the importance of compliance.

Qualifications
• Experience: 5-7 years in IT Audit, IT Compliance, or Cyber Risk.

• Frameworks: Proficiency in applying NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, or COBIT.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure - from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we're building this organisation from the ground up. We're looking for people who'd rather build the playbook than inherit one - who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. About the role

Radiant is looking for an organised, proactive Office Manager to keep our office running smoothly and support the wider team's day-to-day needs. This role blends two things: office management (space, supplies, vendors, facilities) and operations support (scheduling, correspondence, administrative processes). - Manage day-to-day office operations, including supplies, equipment, facilities, and vendor relationships.

- Provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to the operations team and other departments as needed.

- Coordinate scheduling and calendar management for senior staff, including booking meetings, meeting rooms, and travel arrangements.

- Handle the compliance layer that sits under the agreements - liability cover for the spaces we occupy, the health and safety obligations each agreement places on us, DSE and home-working assessments, first aid and fire arrangements.

- Reviewing a vendor or office lease agreement and maintaining a single source of truth for each agreement - term dates, notice periods, break clauses, rent and service charge, desk counts, meeting-room credits, what is included and what is billed on top.

- Own the workplace budget: forecast it, track against it, and give Finance a clear view of committed spend and what is coming up for renewal.

- New joiners: Support onboarding and offboarding of new employees - desk setup, equipment provisioning, welcome packs, and first-day logistics.

- Provide general administrative and operational support to leadership and cross-functional teams as needed.

- Partner with People Team and leadership to align culture initiatives with broader business goals and people strategy

- Continuously review and improve workplace and operational processes to drive efficiency, reduce friction, and enhance the employee experience

- Develop and maintain clear SOPs and playbooks for all core workplace and culture operations, ensuring consistency across sites

 

About You

- Around 5 years of experience in a scale up workplace, office management, people operations, or culture-focused role, ideally within a multi-site environment

title: Data Platform Engineer
description:
Flow Traders is looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform team in our Amsterdam office.

We are a leading proprietary trading firm with an entrepreneurial culture. We value sharp, creative engineers and give them the room and the responsibility to make full use of their abilities.

Your mission is to build and run the platform at the centre of the firm: the source of truth for our proprietary research data, the foundation every department builds on, and the context layer our AI agents depend on. You will make it the place where anyone, human or agent, can find trusted data, understand it, and build on it quickly and safely. Working closely with our Quants and research engineers, you will help shape how the firm does systematic trading.

What you will do

• Own performance at scale. Take ownership of the distributed systems, storage and processing platforms that power our data-intensive applications. You will push them to perform under real market load, from tuning a slow pipeline to designing monitoring and alerting that catches problems before our traders do.

• Build and maintain platform capabilities. Design and maintain the products our users rely on every day: self-provisioned compute, scheduling, transformations, ad-hoc exploration. Treat quants, analysts and other teams as customers of a platform product.

• Make the hard design calls. Be part of the group that shapes the data landscape at Flow Traders. Decide on data modelling, storage formats and processing patterns, weighing performance, cost and maintainability.

• Run what you build. Keep it reliable on busy days, continuously improve resource usage and cost; investigate and resolve data issues and pipeline failures; build operational tooling and runbooks.

• Enable governance and context for AI. Build and maintain the tools that make good governance possible across the firm, such as our data catalog, lineage, access control and configurable data quality rules, and promote their adoption.

• Co-develop with AI, responsibly. Use coding agents daily to design, write, test and review code, while owning the correctness of everything that ships.

• Raise the bar around you. Mentor engineers through code reviews, design discussions and pairing, including how to work effectively and critically with AI tools.

What you need to succeed

Required

• 8+ years building and operating multiple data platforms in production, across different domains. You have made mistakes along the way and can explain what you would do differently.

• You reason from fundamentals (storage layouts, query execution, networking, distributed systems behavior) when designing systems.

• You are comfortable making trade-offs between latency, cost, consistency and simplicity, and can defend them to engineers and business users alike.

• Strong data modelling and data warehousing experience, including analytical engines (e.g. BigQuery, ClickHouse).

• Extensive hands-on experience with distributed storage, messaging (e.g. Kafka, Pub/Sub), batch and stream processing (e.g. Apache Beam, Spark) and container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes).

• Strong programming skills in Python and/or Java, with high standards for testing and code quality.

• Solid cloud experience across storage, databases (e.g. AlloyDB) and data processing, preferably GCP and AWS.

• Practical experience with data governance: ownership, lineage, access control, metadata management and data quality frameworks.

• Understanding of how AI systems consume data (retrieval, semantic layers, tool and agent interfaces) and what it takes to make data reliable context for them.

• You enjoy working with demanding internal users, translating vague needs into clear platform capabilities.

• You communicate clearly across technical and non-technical teams, and you like helping others grow.

• Interest in financial markets is a plus; prior trading experience is not required.

title: Staff Technical Program Manager (f/m/d)
description:
We see the potential inside everything and everyone. Starting with you.

Orbem uses AI to industrialize MRI, delivering non-invasive insight into everything from fruits to eggs to the human body. We are transforming what is becoming the world's largest biological dataset into actionable intelligence to reduce waste, increase quality, and accelerate the shift toward a more sustainable and healthier future.

Headquartered and founded in Munich, Germany, with an office now in Houston, Texas, our world-class team is scaling inside-out technology to transform how humanity sees and understands biological matter.

Help us see what's possible. Join us.

YOUR ROLE

Orbem is at a critical inflection point. As we scale our range of unique products, we need delivery that is predictable, transparent and built to scale.

As a Staff Technical Program Manager within our TPM team, you will drive the delivery of complex, high-stakes programs that bring our products from development to market. You will work across Hardware, Software and Science/AI, aligning teams around shared goals and turning technical complexity into clear plans and decisions.

This is a high-impact role that blends technical depth, delivery architecture and informal leadership. You will work in a complex, fast-scaling environment, and you will also help strengthen how the wider TPM team works.

YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

Own the Execution Plan:

- Architect and design end-to-end delivery plans for your team(s), from initial discovery or design phase until commercial launch.

- Lead quarterly OKR planning and ensure it is fully aligned to company OKRs.

Lead Cross-Functional Coordination:

- Co-lead product delivery with the Product Manager and Tech Leads. You own the how and when.

- Manage dependencies across teams and relevant domains (technical, operations, business development), and keep stakeholders, including external partners, aligned.

Drive Risk & Decision-Making

- Proactively identify, track, and mitigate technical and non-technical risks - timeline, resources, budget, and scope.

- Escalate and resolve cross-team conflicts; create the decision-making frameworks other teams rely on.

Shape Ways of Working

- Champion tooling and process best practices within the team and contribute workflows optimization within the TPM team. (e.g. refine the Product Development Lifecycle, Risk Management processes).

- Coach and mentor other TPMs.

YOUR EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

- Program Leadership: Proven track record managing complex, cross-functional technical programs - ideally spanning hardware, software, and/or AI - with high delivery accountability.

- Technical Depth: Solid understanding of how complex deep-tech products are engineered across Hardware, Software and Science/AI. You can evaluate trade-offs across all three domains well enough to challenge and guide engineering decisions. A technical background in systems engineering, MRI or AI/ML is a plus.

- Practical understanding of how products are operated at customer sites, from early MVPs to mature deployments.

- Execution & Planning: Expert in building and managing master program plans, sprint structures, milestone tracking, and risk registers across multiple concurrent workstreams.

Stakeholder Management: Able to translate technical complexity into executive-level clarity and to influence and align without formal authority across matrixed organizations.

- Change Management: Proven ability to drive adoption of new tools, frameworks, and processes (e.g. PDLC/PLM rollouts, agile tooling) across cross-functional teams - balancing structured change with the pace of a fast-moving scale-up.

- Tooling & Process: Advanced setup of planning and tracking tools such as Jira and Confluence, covering portfolio dashboards, cross-team dependency and risk tracking, and executive-ready reporting. Hands-on with agentic AI tools that boost team efficiency.

- Leadership & Culture: You are a servant leader who thrives in fast-growing scale-up

The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility - and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

As our Mobile Software Engineering Manager on the Audience Technology team, you will lead a highly collaborative team of mobile software engineers building, testing, and delivering award-winning features for NPR's flagship mobile applications. You will partner closely with our Product, Design, Data, and Editorial teams to identify priorities, architect new features, and continuously improve existing applications. title: Recruiting Operations Consultant
description:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

Hi, I’m Casey, Head Customer Success Management and Customer Education at Ashby. I’m thrilled to be hiring our first EMEA-based Recruiting Operations Consultant to support Strategic, Mid-Market, and Startup customers in the EMEA region. In this role, you’ll be part of the Customer Education team, blending 1:1 customer consulting, CSM enablement, and educational content creation to scale advanced recruiting operations expertise, strengthen CSM RecOps literacy, and help customers achieve measurable recruiting outcomes.

You’ll also collaborate with Professional Services to scope and deliver paid consulting engagements (SOWs), helping shape and evolve offerings such as Process Optimization and Fractional RecOps - and, when needed, building reports or processes on behalf of customers to support their goals.

DAY-TO-DAY, THIS LOOKS LIKE:

- Delivering high-impact consulting via RecOps Connects (complimentary 1:1 engagements) and paid engagements, focused on recruiting strategy, analytics interpretation, and operational best practices.

- Partnering with AEs, CSMs, and Professional Services to scope, sell, and deliver paid consulting engagements using the RecOps SOW framework.

- Translating 1:1 consulting insights into scalable education - Academy courses, guides, webinars, and segment-specific playbooks - that go beyond “how” to explain “why.”

- Contributing to advanced product education (e.g., interpreting Quality of Hire dashboards, building analytics strategies) and shaping our most sophisticated Customer Education offerings.

- Partnering closely with the Product Team to distill your observations into tangible feedback.

- Enabling CSMs on foundational RecOps strategies and tactics.

YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

- You have hands-on experience with Ashby’s product and are excited by the power it offers Talent Acquisition teams.

- You love helping customers learn - supporting them as they grow into power users.

- You are an excellent communicator, skilled at clear and concise facilitation.

- You can navigate a range of stakeholders (e.g., Heads of Talent vs. recruiters) and help them align on shared goals.

- You’re comfortable working across a spectrum of complexity - from solving simple interview plan questions to building advanced Quality of Hire reporting strategies.

- You excel at holding stakeholders accountable, setting clear expectations, and facilitating alignment.

- You are proactive about defining boundaries - enabling CSMs to own foundational RecOps work so you can focus on high-leverage contributions.

- You are skilled at enabling others, whether in 1:1 sessions or group settings.

- You have deep empathy for customers and can translate their feedback into actionable insights that shape internal priorities and product direction.

- You have 2+ years experience in recruiting operations, analytics, and process design - and enjoy helping others level up in these areas.

YOU MIGHT NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF:

- You prefer rigid structure and are uncomfortable with ambiguity or evolving priorities.

- You don’t enjoy hands-on building with customers, as this role is a mix of both consulting engagements and build-for-me engagements.

- You are not comfortable running projects from beginning to end, including scoping, execution, and follow-through

- You want to focus exclusively on individual customer conversations and not contribute to scaled education or internal enablement.

- You hesitate to hold customers or internal teams accountable, or avoid facilitating alignment when competing opinions are presented.

- You find it difficult to set boundaries and tend to default to saying “yes” to all requests.

INTERVIEW PROCESS:

- Recruiter Screen with Talent Acquisition Team - 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes

- Take Home / Mock Call - 45 minutes

- Final Panel:

- Interview with CSM Leadership - 30 min

- Interview with CS Senior Leadership - 30 minutes

BENEFITS:

- Competitive salary
